raw_response:
Aiya, what do I plant this year? Same as always, more or less. Me and the old lady, we're both getting on — I'm 63 now, she's not much younger, and the kids moved to the city years ago. Eight mu isn't much, but it's what we've got, and at our age we can't manage more anyway.

I'll do what I've always done. Spring maize on the big field — about six mu of it, the flatter part closer to the road. The other two mu, the strip behind the house, I'll put in mungbean. Mungbean doesn't need much, and we eat some ourselves, sell a bit at the market if the price is any good. Old Wang next door stopped growing mungbean, says it's not worth it, but I like having something different. If the maize has a bad year, at least the mungbean gives us something. And the soil does better when you rotate in a bean crop — my father taught me that.

For the maize, I plant around Grain Rain (谷雨), late April. Can't plant too early, the ground's still cold and the seed just sits there. I buy hybrid seed from the shop in town — the Zhengdan kind or whatever the shop owner says is selling well this year. The seed packets, I can't read them, but the shop owner tells me and I trust him, he's not cheated me yet. Maybe fifty yuan worth per mu.

Fertilizer — I put two bags of compound (复合肥) per mu before planting, same as last year. That's how I've always done it. Two bags. When the maize is up to my knee, if it looks a bit yellow, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. That's enough. Some of the younger farmers put on three bags, but I think that's wasteful, and the money has to come from somewhere. Two bags has given me decent maize for forty years.

Well water for irrigation — I'll water twice most likely. Once after planting if there's no rain, and once at tasseling when the maize really needs it. Pumping costs money, the electric meter runs. If heaven sends rain I skip a watering, save the yuan.

A little herbicide after planting to kill the weeds — at my age I can't hoe six mu by hand anymore. No insecticide unless I see something bad. Usually I don't.

The mungbean, I saved seed from last year's crop. No need to buy. Plant it late May after the spring rains. Barely any fertilizer — maybe half a bag of compound on the whole two mu, just to help it along. Beans make their own feed, everyone knows that. No irrigation, no spray. Harvest in August, pick the pods as they ripen. It's work, bending over, but the old lady helps.

I expect maybe 400 kg per mu of maize if the weather's reasonable. The young business farmers get 500, 550, but they put on more fertilizer and have better seed and irrigate more. I'm happy with 400. Mungbean, maybe 80 kg per mu, nothing special.

The tight part is cash. I've got maybe 3000 yuan set aside for inputs this year, from last year's sales and a bit of pension. I don't want to borrow. I'd rather plant less than go into debt at my age.
